title: [Core] Introduce popleft_n and append_n in FreeKVCacheBlockQueue to further optimize block_pool (#21222)

perf_gain.gain_evidence: ### benchmark scripts - Get new blocks improved from 0.15ms to 0.008ms - Free new blocks improved from 33us to 9us

workload.description: No model, parallelism, dtype, batch size, or sequence length is specified. The PR targets the KV-cache block pool micro-operations directly and evaluates them via microbenchmarks.
workload.evidence: PR evaluated with benchmark scripts and benchmark_blockpool, plus new unit tests for append_n and popleft_n; no serving workload given.

performance.metric: block_pool get_new_blocks and free_blocks latency from benchmark scripts; benchmark_blockpool get_blocks/free_blocks times
performance.evidence: PR Test Result: get new blocks improved from 0.15ms to 0.008ms, free new blocks from 33us to 9us; benchmark_blockpool reported get_blocks and free_blocks times cut in half.

issue_general: A pool of reusable fixed-size memory blocks is kept in a doubly linked list. The system took blocks out one at a time and put them back one at a time. Each single-block operation fixed up neighbor links that were often immediately undone by the next operation, wasting work on a performance-critical path.
solution_general: Add bulk operations that pop or append many blocks in one pass. The links between neighboring blocks are set once, and only the endpoint links to the list's head/tail are fixed once at the end instead of once per block. This roughly halves the pointer operations.
